overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics shows a clear dominance by space, cosmic anomaly, and 'What If' planetary scenario formats. Specifically, titles featuring high-stakes planetary physics, extreme environmental conditions, and extreme scale comparisons (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y with 1,029 views and 38 likes; v1rrcZLdp4U with 1,031 views; A9Qa-RmuOr0 with 981 views) significantly outperform standard biological or psychological facts. Engagement metrics heavily favor interactive or destabilizing thought experiments ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with vivid, bizarre planetary phenomena.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) generated 1,029 views and 38 likes; 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generated 972 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-concept cosmic 'What If' scenarios involving extreme physical states (e.g., supercritical fluids, exotic matter, or extreme gravity wells).

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic Anomalies & Rare Material Worlds
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) pulled 1,031 views; 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) pulled 981 views and 21 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form deep dives into bizarrely extreme astronomical objects that defy common-sense intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (Jc04LVKNd2s) stalled below 20-50 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological micro-facts unless framed through an extreme, high-tension narrative experiment.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' variants received near-zero traction compared to planetary physics.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard textbook biological facts; pivot biology topics exclusively toward cinematic animal survival or extreme physiological adaptations.
